Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1673. MN: Torriani ‘warming up’ as Milan await Maignan’s MRI results

With Mike Maignan suffering an injury on Sunday night, AC Milan are having to prepare in case he’s out for this weekend’s game.

#1670. Germany vs. Netherlands lineups confirmed: Jurgen Klopp, Xavi decisions made for Nations League decider

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:39, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 19:08

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has made two changes to his starting lineup for this evening’s UEFA Nations League decider against the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion in Berlin.

Both changes come in defence, with centre-back Nico Schlotterbeck and left-back Nathaniel Brown coming in to replace Malick Thiaw and Maximilian Mittelstadt respectively.

Schlotterbeck and Brown are joined in a four-man backline by Philipp Treu and Jonathan Tah, protecting Ajax goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Captain Joshua Kimmich will earn his 118th international cap alongside Bayern Munich teammate Aleksandar Pavlovic, with Liverpool playmaker Florian Wirtz operating in the number 10 role.

Brajan Gruda, who along with Wirtz scored in Germany's 3-1 win against Serbia last Friday, retains his starting spot in attack along with Derry Scherhant and centre-forward Kai Havertz.

Germany know that they will climb from third to first position in League A Group B if they beat the Netherlands and Greece fail to beat Serbia, while Klopp's men can secure at least a quarter-final place if they draw in Berlin and Greece lose.

As for the Netherlands, head coach Xavi has made just the one change to the side that began the 7-0 thrashing of Greece in Amsterdam last Friday.

Crystal Palace midfielder Quinten Timber has been recalled at the expense of injured Barcelona star Frenkie de Jong who sustained a back problem against Greece.

This means that Timber and his brother Jurrien Timber of Arsenal – who netted a brace against Greece – will start together for just the second time on the international stage, having previously done so against Greece in October.

In the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Denzel Dumfries will captain the Oranje at right-back, joining Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky Van de Ven and Jurrien Timber in a four-man defence playing in front of goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Quinten Timber will link up with Joey Veerman and Tijjani Reijnders in a three-man midfield, the latter of whom netted a 33-minute first-half hat-trick against Greece.

In-form Roma striker Donyell Malen was also on the scoresheet last time out and will continue to lead the line next to fellow attackers Crysencio Summerville and Cody Gakpo, who scored a 92nd-minute equaliser in the 1-1 draw with Germany in September.

Netherlands head into this contest knowing they will finish top of their group and qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals if they avoid defeat against Germany, while they can also qualify if Greece fail to beat Serbia.

Germany starting lineup: Ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz

Subs: Urbig, Nubel, Thiaw, Baku, Nmecha, Füllkrug, Bischof, Jeltsch, Mittelstadt, El Mala, Karl, Ebnoutalib

Netherlands starting lineup: Verbruggen; Dumfries, Van de Ven; Van Hecke, J. Timber; Q. Timber, Veerman, Reijnders; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo

Subs: Roefs, Flekken, Geertruida, Maatsen, Van den Berg, Kluivert, Meerdink, Til, Lang, Van Bommel, Koopmeiners, Zechiel

Manchester United have reportedly made a key decision on Harry Amass ahead of the January transfer window, as they look to resolve ongoing uncertainty at left-back.

The 19-year-old academy graduate had been linked with a permanent departure from Old Trafford during the summer. However, United now appear ready to protect his future by extending his contract, while leaving open the possibility of another loan move.

With injuries affecting the club’s senior defensive options, Amass’ situation could become increasingly important in the coming months.

According to the Evening Standard, Manchester United are preparing to trigger a 12-month extension clause in Amass’ existing contract.

The decision would give the club greater control over the defender’s future and prevent him from approaching the end of his deal without a resolution.

The club’s latest reported decision suggests they are not ready to lose control of a player who remains a promising defensive prospect.

United’s situation at left-back has been complicated by fitness concerns involving Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

These issues could influence whether Amass stays at Old Trafford or is allowed to leave on loan in January.

United’s reported decision to extend Amass’ contract would provide greater security over his future, but it does not guarantee that he will remain in the first-team squad for the rest of the season.

#1667. Coritiba vs Santos - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 16 Nov 2026 20:01, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 10:52

Coritiba will be looking to move closer to securing their Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A status when they welcome Santos to the Estadio Major Antonio Couto Pereira on Wednesday.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 42 points from 34 matches, five clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors occupy ninth place on 47 points and are hoping to strengthen their push for a place in next season's Copa Libertadores.

Coritiba head into Wednesday's encounter having lost 1-0 away to Internacional in their last league outing, with the defeat preventing them from recording consecutive victories after previously beating Vitoria 2-0 at home.

The result in Porto Alegre extended a difficult period for the Coxa, who have now recorded just one win in their last nine league matches, losing six times and drawing twice during that run.

Coritiba will be keen to make the most of home advantage and take another step towards the 45-point target they have identified for securing top-flight survival, particularly after winning their most recent home fixture.

Guilherme Bossle is expected to remain in interim charge following Fernando Seabra's dismissal, having overseen the victory against Vitoria before the narrow defeat to Internacional, and his immediate priority will be to improve the team's consistency with only three league fixtures remaining after Wednesday's match.

Santos, meanwhile, arrive in Curitiba looking to end a three-match winless run in the league, having drawn with Bahia and Palmeiras before suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Red Bull Bragantino.

The Peixe had briefly improved their position with a 2-1 victory over Fluminense, but they have since struggled to turn promising performances into wins, recording just one victory in their last six league matches (D3, L2), leaving them six points behind sixth-placed Bahia and with ground to make up in the race for continental qualification.

Cuca's side have nevertheless been more productive in front of goal, scoring 50 times in the league, with only five teams finding the net more frequently.

The head-to-head record is another reason for Santos to approach the fixture with confidence, as they have lost only once in the last 10 meetings between the clubs, winning seven and drawing two.

However, Santos were beaten by Coritiba earlier this season, suffering a 3-0 defeat on home soil, although the recent trend in this fixture favours the visitors, with the away team winning three of the last four competitive meetings.

The clubs have also met three times in 2026, including their Copa do Brasil tie, in which Santos progressed after winning 2-0 in Curitiba following a draw in the first leg.

Coritiba will be without goalkeeper Pedro Morisco, who is away with the Brazil national team and is not expected to return to Curitiba in time for Wednesday's fixture, meaning Pedro Rangel is set to start between the posts.

Defender Jacy is also a doubt after suffering a knee problem against Internacional, with the centre-back still undergoing treatment and yet to return to full training, while Lucas Ronier remains unavailable after suffering a serious knee injury.

Santos will welcome back Willian Arao and Gonzalo Escobar, who have recovered from thigh injuries and returned to unrestricted training with the first team.

Thaciano has also resumed working with the squad, although Gabriel Brazao and Lucas Veríssimo remain sidelined, while Alvaro Barreal and Vinicius Lira are also unavailable.

Gabriel Bontempo, Miguelito and Gustavo Caballero have been away on international duty, leaving Cuca with some decisions to make when selecting his squad.

Neymar is available again after having his suspension reduced, while Gabriel Barbosa is expected to lead the attack after scoring 15 goals in the 2026 Campeonato Brasileiro.

Rangel; Tinga, Tiago Coser, Moledo, B. Melo; Gomez, Santos; Lavega, Josue, Lopes; Rocha

Diogenes; Rodinei, Arao, Peres, Escobar; Henrique, Oliva; Coutinho, Neymar, Everton; Barbosa

Coritiba have the advantage of playing at home and will be encouraged by their victory over Santos earlier in the season, but their recent results have been inconsistent.

The visitors have also struggled to win recently, although they still possess enough attacking quality to find the net, making a draw a reasonable outcome.

#1663. Corinthians vs Botafogo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 16 Nov 2026 22:02

Relegation-threatened Corinthians will be looking to climb out of the Brasileirao drop zone when they welcome Copa Sudamericana hopefuls Botafogo to the Neo Quimica Arena this midweek..

The hosts sit 17th in the Brazilian top-flight table after 34 matches, one point behind 16th-placed Internacional, while the visitors are 12th and above 13th-placed Coritiba by virtue of goal difference.

Corinthians ended a 10-match winless league run with victory over Mirassol on matchday 33, and although they failed to secure back-to-back wins following their goalless draw at Sao Paulo last time out, taking a point from that encounter was still an impressive result for a side that had lost each of their previous five league away matches.

The result also means that the Timao have kept consecutive clean sheets after conceding in each of their previous 10 matches during that winless Brasileiro spell, reflecting the improvement in resilience since Clarence Seedorf took over the reins in October.

Fernando Diniz was sacked after the club suffered seven consecutive league defeats, before interim boss William Batista also lost to Palmeiras, but Corinthians have since recorded three results without defeat in four matches under Seedorf's guidance, with the only blemish being a 3-2 setback against Vasco da Gama on October 24.

Knowing that victory this midweek would lift his side temporarily out of the relegation zone, pending Internacional's game against Vasco later on, the former AC Milan midfielder will look to build on the fact that the Timao ended a five-match winless home league run with their victory over Mirassol.

Corinthians have now taken 22 points from their 17 matches at the Neo Quimica Arena in the top-flight campaign, a return that leaves the Sao Paulo-based team with the third-worst home record in the division.

Botafogo, meanwhile, head into this encounter looking to build on their 1-0 victory over Atletico-MG last time out, with Edenilson's 19th-minute goal proving decisive and lifting the Fire into the Copa Sudamericana zone.

The result also ended a two-match losing streak following defeats to Internacional and Remo, while marking Tite's second victory in seven games since his appointment in September and making him the club's third permanent manager of the season after the dismissals of Martin Anselmi and Franclim Carvalho.

Botafogo have now recorded 11 victories from their 34 league matches (D9, L14) this term, scoring 46 goals and conceding 53, meaning there is still room for improvement at both ends of the pitch.

Another victory could lift the Fire as high as 10th, depending on the results of 11th-placed Vasco and 10th-placed Sao Paulo, who both play on Thursday, although Wednesday's visitors are winless in each of their last six away games (D1, L5).

However, Botafogo can draw inspiration from the fact that they are unbeaten in their last five meetings with Corinthians and have recorded victories in three of those outings, including a 3-1 success in the most recent meeting between the two sides.

Corinthians will be without Yuri Alberto, Matheus Pereira and Andre Ramalho, with the first two suspended following their red cards last time out, while the latter is unavailable due to an accumulation of bookings.

Zakaria Labyad and Kayke remain long-term absentees with anterior cruciate ligament injuries, while Rodrigo Garro, Alex Santana, Raniele and former Arsenal defender Gabriel Paulista are working towards full fitness and remain doubtful.

André Luiz will also be unavailable for Corinthians after the CBF rejected the club's request to release him early from Brazil duty, with the midfielder set to remain with the national team for their friendly against Singapore on November 17, just a day before the clash with Botafogo.

Botafogo are expected to be without Nahuel Ferraresi, whose return from international duty could come too late for any major involvement, while Jordan Barrera is ruled out of the season with injury and Danilo is a doubt due to an adductor problem.

Arthur Chaves is still being assessed by the medical department, with Kaio Pantaleao also being targeted for a return after working towards full fitness.

H Souza; Matheuzinho, J Pedro, G Henrique, Angileri; Carrillo, Bidon; Kaio Cesar, Vitinho, Bidu; Depay

Batista; Vitinho, Justino, Marçal, Telles; C Medina, Edenilson; Ziyech, Montoro,  Martins; Soares

Corinthians have the greater need for points and should be motivated by the opportunity to move closer to safety, but their poor home record makes it difficult to back them to claim all three.

Botafogo have been inconsistent in recent weeks, yet their stronger league position and unbeaten run against the hosts suggest that Tite's side can leave Sao Paulo with a share of the points.

#1662. The nine major strategic blunders Ineos have made at Man United that prove they cannot be trusted to choose Michael Carrick's replacement

Published: 21:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 13:20 EST, 11 November 2026

Michael Carrick looks set to pay for Manchester United’s miserable start to the season with his job this week – but removing him won't fix the club's deep-seated problems.

Carrick took more points than any other Premier League manager between his arrival as Ruben Amorim's interim replacement in January and the end of last season.

He was rewarded with the job on a permanent basis but the Carrick era has quickly unravelled and United entered the November international break 18th in the Premier League, out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle and middling at best in the Champions League.

Carrick's dismissal is the latest shameful episode for Ineos, who took control of football decisions in February 2024 when Sir Jim Ratcliffe came on board as a minority owner.

Daily Mail Sport understands CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox still retain Ratcliffe's backing despite being the subject of fan chants calling for their dismissal at recent matches.

Berrada and Wilcox have failed time and time again and yet seem to escape accountability. Here are nine Ineos mistakes that have dragged Manchester United into the unlikeliest of relegation battles – and raise the question of whether they should be trusted to get the next managerial appointment right.

Michael Carrick's dismissal is the latest shameful episode for Ineos, who took control of football decisions in February 2024 when Sir Jim Ratcliffe came on board as a minority owner

Carrick looks set to pay for Manchester United’s miserable start to the season with his job this week – but removing him won't fix the club's deep-seated problems

Erik ten Hag looked to be on thin ice from the moment Ineos walked through the doors at Carrington.

One of his first conversations with the new hierarchy saw the Dutchman offer to put together a plan to overhaul United’s failing data department. The offer was rejected.

‘I offered my knowledge and abilities to Ineos to help them to construct, but they were of the opinion that they already knew everything,’ Ten Hag told The Athletic recently. ‘They were convinced of, say, the philosophy, the strategy, the work methods. But they came from petrochemicals, from Formula 1, from cycling. Top football demands something totally different.’

That summer, Ineos were caught on the hop by the groundswell of support to keep Ten Hag after United beat rivals City in the FA Cup final, when all indications were they had been ready to sack him. Ineos were put in an awkward spot. That said, they still openly flirted with other managers just days after United’s Wembley victory.

Future England boss Thomas Tuchel met with Ratcliffe in Monaco before he dropped out of the race. Gareth Southgate, Mauricio Pochettino, Thomas Frank and Roberto De Zerbi were considered as Ten Hag remained in limbo, all while United navigated the situation without a sporting director or a CEO.

In the end, with tail between legs, an Ineos delegation flew to Ibiza to interrupt Ten Hag’s holiday and agreed to extend his contract by a year, make changes to his coaching staff, as well as make promises for the upcoming transfer market.

Ineos were caught on the hop and kept on Erik ten Hag (right) after United beat rivals City in the FA Cup final, when all indications were they had been ready to sack him

‘They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned,’ Ten Hag explained. ‘We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.’

According to Ten Hag, Ineos went back on their word having said they would not sell Scott McTominay, who joined Napoli that summer for £27.5million, and the manager was sacked 116 days after his deal was extended with another £200m splurged in the transfer window.

By the time Ten Hag was finally dismissed, with a compensation package of £10.4m for him and his coaching staff, Ineos had wasted close to a quarter of a billion through indecision.

Ratcliffe relentlessly pursued Dan Ashworth as he sought an elite sporting director to lead the new sporting structure. He believed the Englishman to be ‘clearly one of the top sporting directors in the world’ and ‘a very capable person’.

Ashworth spent five months on gardening leave after United eventually agreed a near-£3m compensation package with Newcastle United to get him, only to be gone after five months in the North West.

Ratcliffe would go on to blame Ashworth for the decision to stick with Ten Hag and there was a sense that Ashworth was not on board with the move to bring Ruben Amorim in. It all culminated in his shock exit after a 3-2 home defeat by Nottingham Forest in which he was escorted through the press room at Old Trafford with his head bowed en route to a meeting where he was sacked.

Ashworth was paraded as a move that showed Ineos could deliver on their ‘best in class’ mantra, only for them to ditch him embarrassingly quickly.

Dan Ashworth (second right) was paraded as a move that showed Ineos could deliver on their ‘best in class’ mantra, only to embarrassingly ditch him less than six months later

Sir Dave Brailsford, one of Ratcliffe’s most trusted lieutenants, was also an unmitigated disaster. He started off as a crucial figure behind the scenes and his ‘marginal gains’ mantra became a key focus for everyone as he led the renovation of the Carrington training base.

Brailsford drove the appointments of Omar Berrada and Dan Ashworth, and was one of the key men behind ‘Mission 21’, United's bid to win a 21st Premier League title, and ‘Mission 1’, to win a first Women’s Super League title. Both fell under the ‘Project 150’ umbrella he was particularly proud of, to win titles in the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028.

Sixteen months after coming in, Brailsford was removed from day-to-day operations and earlier this year he fully separated from the club by coming off the board.

Brailsford ran football operations at a time of mass redundancies, fans being alienated by ownership, a failing team that produced its worst Premier League finish of 15th, and millions wasted in the transfer market on players that quickly depreciated in value.

Ruthless job cuts, something key Ineos figures have long insisted were essential for the health of the football club, totally destroyed morale and have, according to some remaining staff, completely changed the club for the worse.

In July 2024, staff were told of the need to cut 250 jobs, as company credit cards were cancelled, and staff were asked to contribute towards expenses. In February 2025, Ineos announced a further 150-200 jobs would need to be cut all while austerity measures – the scrapping of free lunches among them – escalated.

All of this against the backdrop of the senior executives continuing to be paid handsomely for gross levels of under-performance.

Having arrived as a technical director working under Ashworth, Wilcox soon found himself thrust into the biggest executive job in the Premier League, as director of football at United.

Omar Berrada (right) is a close friend and supporter of Jason Wilcox (left) and trusts him implicitly, as does Ratcliffe, who believes he has the ‘best eyes’ at the club

He pitched up at United having navigated close to nine months in the same role at Championship side Southampton. Prior to that his expertise had been across at Manchester City in youth development.

Berrada is a close friend and supporter of Wilcox and trusts him implicitly, as does Ratcliffe, who believes he has the ‘best eyes’ at the club. Wilcox was one of the driving forces behind the appointment of Amorim and it was he who would go on to clash with the Portuguese at the end, leading to his eventual sacking.

Wilcox is very hands-on, routinely seen close to training sessions, and has travelled with the team on numerous occasions.

‘When I listen to Jason speak, I get what he’s saying,’ Ratcliffe told The Times in March 2025. ‘He’s a warm character, he’s got a sense of humour, he knows what he’s talking about.’

Wilcox has been accused of interfering too much while not establishing the game model Ineos long promised to implement, regardless of who the head coach is. The director of football was called out in a post-match interview by Lisandro Martinez this season and Wilcox has inexplicably remained in the shadows while players and Carrick face up to the club’s failings.

A patchy recruitment record, all while preparing to search for a third permanent manager in less than 12 months, Wilcox has had next to no positive impact on United’s first team since assuming Ashworth’s job.

Hurting from the way they totally miscalculated and mishandled the Ten Hag situation, Berrada and Wilcox pushed to convince Amorim to abandon Sporting Lisbon mid-season – something he did not want to do – and bring his philosophy to Old Trafford.

It was explained that his 3-4-2-1 system would take a long time to embed onto a squad that had been playing 4-2-3-1 but United's decision-makers were undeterred and forked out £11m to get Amorim and his staff in.

It was explained that Ruben Amorim's 3-4-2-1 system would take a long time to embed but United chiefs were undeterred and forked out £11m to get Amorim and his staff in

A further £250m was spent on the squad the next summer but Amorim's standing took another pounding following a League Cup giantkilling at Grimsby Town

Hiring Amorim in isolation wasn’t an error. He represented a bright young manager that had a clear philosophy – something Ineos haven’t shown in two and a half years – but he had been overlooked by West Ham and Liverpool.

One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that Liverpool compiled a dossier on all the reasons Amorim would not be able to succeed at Anfield, largely down to how many players would need to be recruited to make his vision a successful reality.

Amorim was ‘rewarded’ with just two arrivals in January 2025 in the shape of Patrick Dorgu and Ayden Heaven, while the following summer saw a clash of ideas in terms of transfer targets. Senne Lammens arrived despite Amorim seeking a veteran goalkeeper to replace the hapless Andre Onana.

Amorim guided United to their lowest Premier League finish and lost the Europa League final in Bilbao to Ange Postecoglou’s Tottenham Hotspur. A further £250m was spent on the squad with the attack overhauled but his standing took another pounding following a League Cup giantkilling at Grimsby Town.

Relations between Amorim and Wilcox deteriorated severely and they clashed in a meeting on the eve of the trip to Leeds United, which would prove his final game. Amorim unleashed a fierce rant which intimated that figures such as Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell were overstepping the mark with their input and that they needed to allow him to be the ‘manager’ of the club.

Having come under pressure to change formation and the style of play, Amorim was sacked the morning after drawing at Leeds.

Rather than actually devise a plan to deliver Amorim’s vision, Ineos instead tried to get clever and turned to Harry Marra, a renowned track and field coach, to come in as a consultant.

He was given the remit of assessing individual player running mechanics, acceleration and deceleration. Mason Mount was one of those who Marra identified and he attempted to adjust the 36-cap England midfielder’s running gait.

Ratcliffe imparted advice on stretching techniques he had learned from running the London Marathon to figures in the Carrington physio room

Add from the episode in which Ratcliffe imparted advice on stretching techniques he had learned from running the London Marathon to figures in the Carrington physio room, you got the picture of an ownership that didn’t seem to understand that top-level football isn’t track, field, or cycling.

Performance on the pitch only got worse after this, not better.

8. Prioritising new stadium over a new left back

Speaking to reporters in Dublin this summer shortly after being given the United job full-time, Carrick used the word ‘push’ almost a dozen times when referencing what the club still had to do in the transfer market.

But Ineos, again believing they are the smartest people in the room, ignored those pleas and stuck to their plan to ‘fix’ one part of the team per summer. It was the attack in 2025, and in 2026 it would be the midfield, with the defence to come next year.

So, despite knowing full well that expecting another injury-free campaign from Luke Shaw was an enormous gamble, they did it anyway and made no defensive reinforcements. It hasn’t taken long for that move to backfire spectacularly.

Instead, the decision was made to purchase land to the tune of £60m so they can plough on with plans for a swanky new 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North' stadium that many fans believe will never be built.

Rather than fixing the team's defence, United chiefs spent £60m on a slither of land to progress with their plans for a 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North'

The way Carrick has been treated in this whole saga has been cruel and a sign of why managers should think twice about taking a job under Ineos

An emergency meeting after a 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last month looked set to be the end for Carrick until Berrada, Wilcox, Ratcliffe and the Glazers surprised the football world and simply did nothing. Everyone just continued with business as usual with no backing for the beleaguered Carrick.

Defeat at Chelsea, coupled with two frantic displays to come from 2-0 down against both Roma and Aston Villa followed. Then came the revelation on Monday that Berrada and Wilcox had settled on a recommendation to the board that they should sack Carrick. But instead of being sanctioned immediately, Carrick spent seven hours at Carrington on Tuesday to take training and watch an Under 17s match.

We are told yet again that Carrick's future will finally be decided on Wednesday at a meeting in Monaco, but in the meantime he must carry on until he gets wind he has been officially sacked.

The way Carrick has been treated in this whole saga has been cruel and a sign of just why managers should – and will – think twice about taking a job under Ineos.

#1661. Arsenal targeting Nicolo Tresoldi as potential Viktor Gyökeres replacement

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Arsenal’s attacking plans could be heading towards a significant change as questions emerge over Viktor Gyökeres’ future at the Emirates Stadium.

With the Gunners continuing to assess their options at centre-forward, a rising star in Belgian football has reportedly emerged as a potential alternative.

Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi is attracting growing interest from across the Premier League after an impressive run in front of goal.

Arsenal are among the clubs monitoring the German forward, who could become a target if Mikel Arteta’s side decide to reshape their attacking options.

According to TEAMtalk, Arsenal had representatives watching Tresoldi during Club Brugge’s recent victory over St Truiden, in which the 22-year-old scored a hat-trick.

Chelsea, Manchester City, Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United were also represented, highlighting the competition Arsenal could face.

Tresoldi has enjoyed a prolific spell in Belgium, with his goalscoring performances strengthening his reputation as one of Europe’s promising young forwards. Reports have suggested that Arsenal are considering him as a possible replacement for Gyökeres, whose future has come under scrutiny following a difficult start to the campaign.

Gyökeres arrived at Arsenal with high expectations, but uncertainty surrounding his role has fuelled speculation about whether the club could consider a change in attack. Tresoldi’s recent form has reportedly put him on the radar as a potential option, although there is no guarantee that Arsenal will move to sell their Swedish striker or make a formal bid for the Brugge forward.

Any deal would also be complicated by Club Brugge’s stance. TEAMtalk reports that the Belgian club have no intention of selling Tresoldi in January and would demand a club-record fee exceeding €40 million to consider his departure.

With several Premier League sides monitoring his progress, Arsenal could face a competitive and expensive transfer battle if they decide to pursue him.

Tresoldi represents a potential long-term option for Arsenal if the club decide to reassess their centre-forward position. His goalscoring form has attracted attention, but moving from Belgian football to the Premier League would present a different challenge, particularly if he were expected to lead the line for a title-chasing side.

Arsenal must also weigh the financial implications of a deal against the uncertainty surrounding Gyökeres’ future. Signing Tresoldi would require a substantial investment, and Club Brugge’s determination to keep him until at least the end of the season makes a January move difficult.

For now, Arsenal’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing their attacking options rather than confirming a change is imminent. If Gyökeres’ situation develops and Tresoldi maintains his impressive form, the young striker could become one to watch in Arsenal’s future transfer plans.

#1660. “Being talked about…”: Everton plotting January move for “interesting” England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1659. Remo vs Chapecoense - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 22:21

The two bottom clubs in the Brasileiro Serie A face off on Wednesday, with Remo still fighting for survival when they take on Chapecoense at the Mangueirao.

The Belem-based club sit 19th in the table with 29 points and will need a herculean effort over the closing stages of the campaign to avoid joining Chapecoense in Serie B next season.

As things stand, Remo are eight points adrift of both Corinthians and Gremio with just four matches remaining, making their chances of survival increasingly remote.

It has been a dreadful campaign for Thiago Carpini's side, who have conceded 57 goals this season, with only Chapecoense shipping more.

The Blue Lion have managed just four wins all season and collected only 19 points, the second-lowest tally in the league, offering little encouragement in their bid to avoid relegation.

However, Remo can take confidence from their 3-2 victory over Chapecoense in the reverse fixture and are unbeaten against their opponents in their last three meetings.

The hosts have suffered six defeats in their last 10 matches, although they did claim a 2-1 victory over Botafogo in their most recent home outing.

Chapecoense's return to the top flight has been far from memorable, with their relegation already confirmed as they prepare for an immediate return to Serie B next season.

It has been a wretched campaign for the Big Green, who have struggled to compete at the highest level and managed just four victories all season.

Rodrigo Vicenzi Casarin's side have scored only 33 goals in the league, the fewest of any team, while conceding 70.

Their away record has been equally dismal, with just one win and seven points from 17 matches, during which they have shipped 32 goals.

Chapecoense have lost their last three matches and six of their previous seven, with little left to play for as they look to bring their losing run to an end.

Remo will be without captain Marllon for this encounter due to an accumulation of yellow cards, while several other players are also struggling with injuries.

Gabriel Poveda is nursing a thigh problem, while Jaderson and Matheus Felipe are dealing with similar issues. Defender Joao Lucas is also sidelined with a meniscus injury.

Chapecoense have been without versatile forward Mauricio Garcez since late October due to a leg injury, and he is expected to return at some point this month.

Aside from Garcez, their only other absentee is Rafael Carvalheira, who will miss the remainder of the season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

#1653. Chelsea and Manchester United lead race for Barcelona Fermin Lopez

By Alexis Pereira | 16 Nov 2026 23:37

Barcelona have reportedly received offers of up to £85m from the Premier League for Fermin Lopez, but the Spain midfielder wants to stay at Camp Nou and the club are preparing to discuss a new contract with his representatives. According to Sport, Chelsea and Manchester United are the two clubs most determined to sign the 23-year-old.

Long regarded as a promising player capable of bringing energy and drive off the bench, the attacking midfielder has gradually established himself as an important part of boss Hansi Flick’s system. His performances in recent months, particularly his two goals against Atletico Madrid, have strengthened his status further. At 23, he already has eight goals and seven assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

His ability to get into the box, attack space from the second line and make a difference in the final 30 metres makes him a particularly valuable weapon for Barcelona. Lopez also brings strong intensity to the press and a verticality that complements the more organising midfielders in the Catalan squad. Unsurprisingly, the progress has not gone unnoticed in the transfer market, and several English clubs appear ready to invest heavily to persuade him to move.

According to Sport, Barcelona have received proposals from the Premier League for the attacking midfielder. Some reach £85m, a considerable amount that reflects the growing value of the Spain international, who has 12 caps. Chelsea and Manchester United are the two sides most determined to sign him, while the identity of the other two suitors has not been revealed.

Chelsea’s interest is not new. The London club tried in the last summer window with a proposal estimated at £59.5m, which did not even lead to real discussions with the Catalan hierarchy. This time the figures mentioned are much higher and leave Barcelona with an important decision to make.

From a sporting point of view, losing such a decisive and versatile player would be difficult to replace. Financially, however, a £85m fee could give interesting room for manoeuvre to a board that remains mindful of its economic constraints. It remains to be seen whether the club are genuinely willing to listen to such offers.

Barcelona’s main argument for keeping him may also be the most important: Lopez does not want to leave. He is strongly attached to the club, where he wants to keep progressing and put down roots, and he is not particularly tempted by approaches from the Premier League. The number seven has even said he wishes to end his career in Catalonia.

That position makes the sporting department’s job easier. According to Sport, Barcelona plan to meet his representatives soon to discuss a new contract improvement, with the aim of raising his salary to reflect his new status in Flick’s squad.

Lopez already extended his contract until 2031 in January 2026 and has a release clause of £425m. The Catalan club intend to keep protecting one of their most valuable assets, and in the face of the English millions, Barcelona seem to be considering a reward for their rising star rather than a departure.

#1651. Defender David Bates recalled by Scotland after almost eight-year absence

Published: 13:34 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 13:45 EST, 11 November 2026

David Bates has been rewarded for a strong start to life in Turkey by earning a recall to the Scotland squad almost eight years after his last appearance for the national team.

The 30-year-old centre-back has been added to Sebastien Pocognoli’s group after Luis Binks withdrew ahead of the Nations League matches against North Macedonia on Friday and Switzerland on Monday.

Bates currently plays for Amedspor and has started all 11 matches this season as his club have soared to third in the Turkish Super Lig.

The defender won all four of his caps under Alex McLeish while playing for Hamburg in the 2018/19 campaign. His last appearance for the national team was in a 2-0 win over San Marino in a Euro 2020 qualifier in March 2019, in what also turned out to be McLeish’s last game in charge.

Former Rangers player Bates joined Amedspor in the summer after spending four years in Belgium with Mechelen and then Standard Liege following his Aberdeen exit in 2022.

Brondby captain Binks is the second centre-back to drop out of the squad initially named by Pocognoli last week, after Swansea’s Stephen Welsh sustained an injury and had to be replaced by Los Angeles FC’s Ryan Porteous last weekend.

David Bates playing for Scotland against Albania back in 2018

Sebastian Pocognoli is keen to create a winning culture in the Scotland squad

The head coach is viewing this month’s double-header as crucial to his preparations for the Euro 2028 qualification campaign, which could begin in March if Scotland are not involved in Nations League play-offs.

'I think that these two games are, if we start the qualification in March, the last package of games that we have to use to be ready for the March camp,' Pocognoli said.

'If it’s not the case (that the Euro campaign starts in March), we can play friendly games which can be useful for June, so we have more time to prepare. And maybe, if we are really strong in the next two games, maybe we have play-off games. That’s the ambition.

'These can be useful also for the process of the qualification. But if the qualification starts (in March), we need to be ready. That’s why this camp for me is crucial in terms of demanding to the players, try to impress me and do everything to improve.

'I believe if we want to go to the Euros and be successful, we need to build this qualification feeling by winning games and to build the best winning culture possible.'

Chelsea are continuing to assess their defensive options as they plan for future transfer windows, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a player attracting attention.

The 21-year-old has impressed in Italy, and his performances have reportedly placed him on Chelsea’s recruitment radar.

According to the Mail Online, the Blues are keeping track of his development as they consider potential additions to their defence.

Ramon has attracted interest after establishing himself at Como. His performances have reportedly caught the attention of several major clubs, with Chelsea among those monitoring his progress.

However, securing his signature may prove complicated because of Real Madrid’s contractual position. The Spanish giants are understood to have retained buy-back and sell-on clauses when Ramon left the club for Como.

Those provisions could give Madrid considerable influence over the defender’s future and potentially make negotiations more difficult for interested clubs.

Chelsea are also likely to face competition from Arsenal and Manchester United, who have reportedly been linked with the young centre-back.

Ramon represents a potential long-term defensive addition for Chelsea as the club looks to maintain depth and quality at the back.

His development in Serie A makes him an interesting option, but Chelsea would need to navigate Real Madrid’s contractual rights and competition from other Premier League sides.

For now, the reported interest appears to be part of Chelsea’s wider recruitment monitoring rather than evidence of a formal bid or advanced negotiations.

#1646. Liverpool step up pursuit of 21-year-old Russia international amid interest from Barcelona and PSG

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Liverpool continue to assess potential additions to their attacking options as the club looks towards future transfer windows. One name attracting attention is Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, although the Reds could face serious competition from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

The 21-year-old has made an impressive start to life in Turkey following his summer move from Lokomotiv Moscow.

His performances have reportedly caught Liverpool’s attention, but Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are also keeping tabs on his situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Liverpool and Arsenal have stepped up their interest in Batrakov after sending scouts to watch him during Galatasaray’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Lille. The Russian midfielder found the net in that match, further strengthening his growing reputation.

Liverpool are not alone in monitoring the youngster. Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City have also been credited with interest, while Barcelona and PSG remain potential destinations.

Batrakov joined Galatasaray from Lokomotiv Moscow in August for €25million and has quickly made an impact. The attacking midfielder has reportedly contributed goals in European competition, with his technical quality, creativity and ability to threaten the opposition goal making him an attractive prospect.

One of the most significant details surrounding his future is a reported release clause worth around £50million. The clause is understood to allow him to leave Galatasaray for a club in one of Europe’s top four leagues, potentially giving Liverpool a clear route to pursuing a deal.

However, Galatasaray are reportedly pleased with their summer signing and have little desire to sell him so soon after his arrival.

TEAMtalk also reports that Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, while PSG continue to be viewed as a possible destination. Both clubs could offer strong competition if Liverpool decide to turn their scouting interest into a concrete move.

For Liverpool, Batrakov represents a potential opportunity to secure a highly regarded young attacking midfielder with considerable room for development. His creativity and goal threat could make him an interesting option as the club continues to assess its long-term attacking plans.

The reported £50million release clause provides some clarity over the financial side of a possible transfer. Nevertheless, Liverpool would still need to convince the player that Anfield is the right destination, particularly with Barcelona and PSG reportedly capable of appealing to him.

A January move appears less realistic, with Galatasaray having little interest in losing a player they only signed in the summer. A deal next summer could be a more plausible scenario if Liverpool maintain their interest.

For now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

#1645. Gremio vs Bahia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 05:14

Gremio will host Bahia at their Arena do Gremio home in Porto Alegre on Wednesday night, for a crucial showdown that will have ramifications for both the Brasileirao's relegation battle and race for Copa Libertadores qualification.

The Tricolor dos Pampas are hoping to build on their cup success last time out, while the Steel Squad are keen to bounce back from defeat.

Renato Portaluppi's Gremio have endured a dire league campaign so far, but they are far from doomed in the Brazilian top flight.

The Tricolor dos Pampas held Athletico Mineiro to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their Copa do Brasil semi-final on November 7, earning a 3-1 aggregate victory and a place in the final against Palmeiras.

In the Brasileirao, Portaluppi's side are currently 18th with 37 points to their name, sitting in the relegation zone with just four games to play.

However, Gremio are only one point shy of 16th-placed Internacional and 15th-placed Vitoria, giving the team genuine hope as the season enters its final stretch.

This week's hosts will also be buoyed by the fact they have lost just one of their last four home matches across all competitions, beating Mineiro 2-0 in the first leg of their cup tie after another 2-0 triumph over Athletico Paranaense in the league.

Meanwhile, Rogerio Ceni's Bahia are pushing for a place in the Copa Libertadores next term, and are currently in position to make the qualifiers, though the pressure is mounting.

The Steel Squad are sixth with 53 points, and with four matches remaining on their calendar, they sit one point short of fifth-placed Athletico Paranaense, and four behind fourth-placed Fluminense, who occupy one of the automatic entry spots.

That being said, Bahia's ambitions took a hit last time out on November 6, when they were downed 3-2 by Cruzeiro, who came from behind to win on a disappointing evening in Belo Horizonte.

As a result, Ceni's men are now within reach of seventh-placed Mineiro, who are a mere two points back in seventh after their goalless draw with Mirassol on Saturday.

To make matters worse, the visitors come into this clash having lost three of their past four away games, drawing once - a 1-1 stalemate with Santos late last month.

On the other hand, Bahia have played one match fewer than Mineiro, and Wednesday night represents a chance for them to strengthen their cushion over their rivals in the race for Libertadores qualification.

Gremio are without midfielders Mathias Villasanti (suspended), Juan Nardoni (thigh) and Danilo (muscle), though Dodi and Filip Krovinovic should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Walter Kannemann is also suspended for accumulating yellow cards, while right-back options Diego Caito and Cristian Pavon are sidelined due to respective muscle injuries.

In their absence, Gustavo Martins, Wallace and Fabian Balbuena look set to start in a three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Joao Pedro and Marlon.

As for Bahia, they are missing goalkeeper Leo Vieira, who is out for the season with a knee injury, while centre-half Marco Moreno is a doubt with stomach trouble.

If the latter is unavailable, then David Duarte and Kanu should be ready to start in front of shot-stopper Ronaldo.

Weverton; Martins, Wallace, Balbuena; Pedro, Dodi, Krovinovic, Marlon; Enamorado, Vinicius, Amuzu

Ronaldo; Victor, Duarte, Kanu, Juba; Erick, Acevedo, Nestor; Oliveira, Veliz, Pulga

Gremio may be in the relegation zone, but they arrive in better form than their opponents and will be optimistic about delivering a strong performance.

However, Bahia will be motivated by the race for Libertadores action, and are unlikely to be beaten again after their frustrating defeat last time out.

#1644. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

"He's important for us"Virgil van Dijk says Cody Gakpo will be important for Liverpool this season after the win over Ipswich 💪 pic.twitter.com/XLWfxbpK2d

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

2 - Liverpool have now won as many Premier League away games by 2+ goals this season (1) as they did in the whole of last season (2-0 v West Ham in November 2025).Lift-off. pic.twitter.com/rp39p6C8z5
