a, Heatmap of genes differentially expressed in BA-L cells and BA-H cells in BAT, with H6pd, Rgs2, and Ucp1 highlighted with a red asterisk. Data were obtained from the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) (accession GSE125269). b, Heatmap of genes related to thermogenesis and GR signalling that are differentially expressed in BA-L cells and BA-H cells, with Ucp1 and H6pd highlighted in red. c, Top pathway enrichment analysis for BA-L cells compared with BA-H cells, including upregulated and downregulated biological processes, with glucocorticoid-related pathways highlighted in red. The “Gene Ratio” represents the ratio of the number of input (differentially expressed) genes associated with a given pathway to the total number of input genes. p-values are shown in standard scientific notation; dot colour indicates the adjusted p-values (the brighter red indicating greater significance), and the dot size reflects the number of enriched genes. d, UMAP plots of the adipocyte fraction from BAT of WT mice maintained at room temperature. e, Distribution of the expression of Ucp1, Cox6b1, H6pd, Rgs2, Txnip and Nr3c1 within UMAP plots. f, Violin plots showing the expression and distribution of Ucp1, Cox6b1, H6pd, Rgs2, Txnip and Nr3c1.

a, The Ucp1-Chaser-mTmG mouse model is generated by crossing Ucp1-rtTA transgenic mice with TRE-Cre and Rosa26-loxP-STOP-loxP-mT/mG transgenic mice. In Ucp1-Chaser-mTmG mice, all cells express tdTomato. When mice are put on a doxycycline diet, UCP1-high-expressing cells will start rtTA expression; rtTA will then bind to the TRE promoter, inducing Cre expression. Cre will specifically excise the floxed membrane-localizing Tomato (mTomato) sequence, initiating expression of membrane-localizing GFP (mGFP). b, BA-L cells and BA-H cells were freshly isolated from the BAT of WT mice. H6PD and UCP1 immunoblots and quantification normalized to Ponceau S staining. Representative Ponceau S-stained membrane as shown as loading controls. n = 4 per group. c, SVFs and BAs were freshly isolated from the BAT of WT mice. PDGFRα, UCP1, H6PD, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification. n = 4 per group. d, Ucp1-mGFP knock-in (KI) generation strategy: A P2A-mGFP cassette was inserted into the 5′ end of 3′UTR, immediately upstream of the STOP codon of Ucp1 gene. e, Representative GFP fluorescent images of whole BAT from 10-week-old male Ucp1-mGFP (left) and WT (right) littermates, demonstrating GFP expression exclusively in Ucp1-mGFP mice. f, GFP, UCP1, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification in whole BAT from 10-week-old male Ucp1-mGFP mice and WT littermates. n = 6 per group. g, IF staining showing the pattern of GFP (green) expression in the BAT of 10-week-old male Ucp1-mGFP mice. h, IF staining for GFP (green), H6PD (red), perilipin (white), and DAPI (blue) in vitro-differentiated brown adipocytes and beige adipocytes derived from Ucp1-mGFP mice BAT SVFs and iWAT SVFs. Statistics were computed by unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test [b, f (UCP1)] or unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test [c, f (GFP)]. **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For b, c, and f, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, 10-week-old Male WT mice were housed at 24 °C or 6 °C for 1, 3 or 7 days. TNAP, CKB, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification in BAT. n = 4 per group. b, TNAP, CKB, GR, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification in freshly isolated primary BA-L cells and BA-H cells from 10-week-old male WT mice. n = 3 per group. c, Representative IF staining for H6PD (red), TNAP (green), DAPI (blue), merged with autofluorescence signal (white), in BAT from 10-week-old male WT mice housed at 24 °C. Quantification of the relative percentage of BAs positive for H6PD+ only, TNAP+ only, or both. n = 4 per group. d, Representative IF staining for H6PD (red), TNAP (green), DAPI (blue), merged with autofluorescence signal (white), in iWAT from 10-week-old male WT mice housed at 6 °C for 7 days. Quantification of the relative percentage of multilocular beige adipocytes positive for H6PD+ only, TNAP+ only, or both. n = 4 per group. e, Representative images of IF staining for GFP (green), TNAP (red), perilipin (white), and DAPI (blue) in BAs differentiated from BAT SVFs. Statistics were computed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (a, c, d) or unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test (b). *p < 0.05, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For a–d, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, Freshly isolated BA-H cells and BA-L cells (1 × 105 cells) from 10-week-old male WT mice were incubated with either 5 mM [U-13C] glucose or 0.5 mM [U-13C] palmitate tracing media for 2 h and 6 h. Illustration of carbon transition from extracellular glucose and palmitate. n = 3 per group. b, The relative abundance of fully labelled (m + 16) free palmitate C16:0 in BA-H cells and BA-L cells cultured with [U-13C] palmitate at 2 h. n = 3 per group. c, The relative abundance of fully labelled (m + 16) total palmitate C16:0 in BA-H cells and BA-L cells cultured with [U-13C] palmitate at 2 h. n = 3 per group. d, The citrate enrichment shows the glucose oxidation and fatty acid oxidation in BA subpopulations at 2 or 6 h (2 h, 6 h). n = 3 per group. e, f, 10-week-old male Ucp1-mGFP mice were injected with lentivirus overexpressing H6pd or mCherry as a control in BAT. After 2 weeks of recovery. Representative IF staining for H6PD (green), perilipin (red), and DAPI (blue) in BAT (e). Representative IF staining for mCherry (green), perilipin (red), and DAPI (blue) in BAT (f). Statistics were computed by unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test (b), unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test (c), or two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (d). *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For b–d, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, BAs differentiated from the BAT SVFs from WT mice were pretreated with 1 μM DEX for 12 h, followed by 10 μM CL-316,243 treatment for 24 h. RT–qPCR analysis of Ucp1 mRNA levels. n = 3 per group. b–d, BAs differentiated from the primary BAT SVFs from Ucp1-mGFP mice were cultured with or without DEX, 11-DHC, or CORT throughout the adipogenic differentiation period. GFP fluorescence reflects real-time UCP1 (green) and perilipin (red) expression (b). Quantification of GPF+ BA-H percentage (c). RT–qPCR analysis of mRNA levels of Ucp1, Pparg, and Fabp4 (d). n = 4 per group for (c) and n = 3 per group for (d). e, f, 10-week-old male WT mice were injected with vehicle or DEX for 2 weeks. H&E and IF staining for UCP1 (green), perilipin (red), and DAPI (blue) in BAT (e). Quantification of BA-H percentage (f). n = 4 per group. g, h, IF staining for GFP (green), RGS2 (red), perilipin (white), and DAPI (blue) in BAs differentiated from BAT SVFs of Ucp1-mGFP mice (g) or beige adipocytes differentiated from iWAT SVFs of Ucp1-mGFP mice (h). i, GR binding at the Rgs2 locus in white adipocytes visualized by IGV. Data sourced from the study by Soccio et al.29. j, k, In vitro-differentiated BAs from the primary BAT SVFs from WT mice were reverse-transfected with Rgs2 or control DsiRNAs. 2 days post-transfection, BAs were treated with vehicle or NA for 30 min. Phosphorylated PKA substrate and β-actin immunoblot (j) and quantification (k). n = 4 per group. Statistics were computed by two-way ANOVA with factors for DEX and CL-316,243 treatment, followed by Fisher’s LSD multiple-comparisons test (a), one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (c, d, k) or unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test (f). **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For a, c, d, f, and k, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 6 °C, 24 °C, or 30 °C for 7 days. UCP1, H6PD, GR, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification. n = 3 per group. b, c, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 24 °C or 6 °C for 1, 3 or 7 days. H6PD, UCP1, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification in iWAT (b) and gWAT (c). n = 4 per group. d, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 30 °C for 1 week, followed by i.p. injections with vehicle or CL-316,243 (1 mg kg−1), and an additional week of housing at 30 °C. H6PD, UCP1, GR, and β-actin immunoblots and quantification. n = 4 per group. e, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 6, 24, or 30 °C for 7 days. RT–qPCR analysis of mRNA levels of Ucp1 and H6pd in BAT. n = 5 per group. f, g, 8-week-old Ucp1-Chaser-mTmG male mice underwent sham surgery or unilateral denervation of BAT. After 2 weeks of recovery, mice were housed at 24 °C or 6 °C for 1 week (with doxycycline treatment in f). (f) H&E staining of BAT. (g) RT–qPCR analysis of mRNA levels of glucocorticoid signalling target genes in BAT. n = 4 per group. h, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 6 °C for 1 week or housed at 6 °C for 1 week and then 30 °C for 1 week. RT–qPCR analysis of mRNA levels of glucocorticoid signalling target genes in BAT under different temperature conditions. n = 4 per group. i–p, 10-week-old male Ucp1-rtTA/TRE-cre/Nr3c1flox/flox or control littermates were fed a doxycycline diet at 6 °C for 1 week, followed by 1 week at 24 °C with continued dox diet treatment. Oxygen consumption (i), RER (j), physical activity (k), and food intake (l) were measured by the metabolic cage. Fat (m) and lean (n) compositions were measured by NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance). Glucose tolerance test (o) and insulin tolerance test (p) were conducted in another cohort. n = 7 per group for (i-n) and n = 4 per group for (o, p). Statistics were computed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (a, b (H6PD), c, e), one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s T3 multiple-comparisons test (b (UCP1)), unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test [d, h, i (Average), l–n], unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test [h (Txnip)], two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (g), or two-way ANOVA with Šídák’s multiple comparisons test [i (time-course curves and Day/Night), j, k, o, p]. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For a–e, and g–p, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, 8-week-old male WT mice underwent sham surgery or unilateral denervation of BAT. After 2 weeks of recovery, mice were housed at 24 °C or 6 °C for a week. RT–qPCR analysis cytokine gene expression in BAT. n = 4 per group. b, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed in 6 °C for 1 week or housed in 6 °C for 1 week and then 30 °C for 1 week. RT–qPCR analysis cytokine gene expression in BAT. n = 4 per group. c, RT–qPCR analysis of Il1b and Tnfa mRNA levels in BAT explants incubated with vehicle or NA. n = 4 per group. d, Serum IL-1β levels measured by ELISA in 10-week-old male WT mice housed at 30 °C, 24 °C, or 6 °C for 1 or 3 days. n = 8 per group. e, f, 8-week-old male Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice underwent sham surgery or unilateral denervation of BAT. After 2 weeks of recovery, mice were housed at 24 °C or 6 °C with doxycycline treatment for 1 week. Representative IF staining for GFP (green), IL-1β (purple), and DAPI (blue) in BAT (e). The yellow dashed lines circle the BA-L (GFP−) clusters, where IL-1β puncta are enriched; the yellow solid lines circle the BA-H (GFP+) clusters, where IL-1β puncta are not enriched. Pearson correlation coefficient of co-localization between UCP1 and IL-1β (f). n = 4 per group. g, RT–qPCR analysis of H6pd and Nr3c1 mRNA levels. n = 3 per group. h, i, BAs differentiated from primary BAT SVFs of WT mice were pretreated with the following inhibitors: BAY11-7082 (NF-κB inhibitor, 5 µM), Aspirin (IκB inhibitor, 5 µM), SB203580 (p38 MAPK inhibitor, 10 µM), SP600125 (JNK inhibitor, 10 µM), or U0126 (MEK/ERK inhibitor, 10 µM) for 30 min, followed by IL-1β treatment (10 ng ml−1) for 48 h. H6PD and β-actin immunoblots (h) and quantification (i). n = 4 per group. j, k, BAs differentiated from primary BAT SVFs of WT mice were switched on day 6 to culture medium containing charcoal-stripped FBS (lacking basal corticosterone) and then treated with vehicle or 10 ng ml−1 IL-1β for 48 h in the absence (j) or presence (k) of 1 μM 11-DHC. UCP1 and β-actin immunoblots and quantification. n = 4 per group. l, m, Ucp1-Chaser-mTmG male mice were maintained on standard chow until 8 weeks of age, then switched to a doxycycline chow diet for 3 days at 24 °C. BAT was processed using the Adipo-Clear method and immunolabeled for GFP (green) with the synaptic marker synaptophysin (red) (l) or sympathetic neuron marker tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) (red) (m). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments. Statistics were computed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (a, d, g), two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (i), unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test [b (Tnfa)], or unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test [b (all other genes), c, j, k]. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. For a–d, and f–k, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, t-SNE plots of the non-adipocyte fraction from BAT of C57BL/6J mice maintained at room temperature. Data were sourced from the NCBI GEO database under identifiers GSE207707, GSE177635, GSE160585, and GSE161447. b, t-SNE plots displaying the expression and distribution of Ptprc, Adrb1, Adrb2, and Adrb3 genes in BAT non-adipocyte fraction. c, t-SNE plots of immune cells from BAT of C57BL/6J mice maintained at room temperature. Immune cell clusters were identified based on the expression of Ptprc and were filtered to exclude contaminating erythrocytes (Hba-a1, Hba-a2), capillary endothelial cells (Pecam1, Gpibp1), smooth muscle cells (Acta2), and adipose progenitor cells (Pdgfra, Col3a1). Data was sourced from the NCBI GEO database under identifiers GSE207707, GSE177635, GSE160585, and GSE161447. d, e, t-SNE plots displaying the expression and distribution Il1b genes (d) and Ptprc (CD45, immune cells), Cd19 (CD19, B cells), Cd3e (CD3, T cells), Itgam (Integrin alpha M, CD11b, Myeloid cells), Lyz2 (Lysozyme 2, LyZ2, Myeloid cells), Adgre1 (Adhesion G protein-coupled receptor E1, F4/80, Macrophages), Mrc1 (Mannose receptor, c type 1, CD206, anti-inflammatory macrophages), Ly6g (Lympthocyte antigen 6 complex, locus G, Ly6G, Neutrophils), Csf3r (Colony stimulating factor 3 receptor, G-CSFR, Neutrophils), Cxcr2 (Chemokine (C-X-C motif) receptor 2, CXCR2, Neutrophils), Ly6c1 (Lympthocyte antigen 6 complex, locus C1, Ly6C, Monocytes) in BAT immune cells (e).

a, Flow cytometry gating strategy for CD45+, T cell, and B cell in BAT SVFs from 10-week-old male WT mice. Doublets and nonviable cells were excluded, followed by gating on CD45+ lymphocytes. T cells and B cells were subsequently selected based on CD3+ or CD19+ expression. b, Percentage of IL-1β+ cells within CD45+ lymphocytes and CD45− non-immune cells. c, Flow cytometry gating strategy for neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages. Doublets and nonviable cells were excluded from SVFs, followed by gating on CD45+ CD11b+ myeloid. Macrophages were identified by F4/80+ expression, while F4/80− cells were further classified as neutrophils and monocytes based on CXCR2+ and Ly6C+ expression. d, Percentage of IL-1β+ cells within each immune cell type, including macrophage, neutrophils, monocytes, B cells, and T cells. n = 6 per group. e, Absolute number of IL-1β+ cells per gram of brown adipose tissue within each immune cell type. n = 3 per group. f, g, Representative images of IF staining for CXCR2 (red) or F4/80 (red), IL-1β (green), and DAPI (blue) in BAT. h–j, BAs differentiated from primary BAT SVFs, with or without CD45+ immune cells, from Ucp1-mGFP mice. GFP fluorescence reflects real-time UCP1 expression in the brightfield images. Representative IF staining for GFP (green), perilipin (red), and DAPI (blue) (h). Quantification of GPF+ BA-H percentage (i). RT–qPCR analysis of Pparg and Fabp4 mRNA levels (j). n = 3 per group for (i) and n = 4 per group for (j). Statisticswere computed by unpaired two-tailed Welch’s t-test (b), unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test (i, j), or one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (d, e). **p < 0.01, ****p < 0.0001. For b, d, e, i, and j, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, 10-week-old male Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice were injected with lentivirus overexpressing IL-1RA or mCherry (control) into BAT. Following a 2-week recovery period, mice were housed at 24 °C with doxycycline treatment for a week. Representative images of IF staining for IL-1RA (red), GFP (green), perilipin (white), and DAPI (blue) in BAT. b, BAs differentiated from the primary BAT SVFs from WT mice were reverse-transfected with Il1r1 or control DsiRNAs. 2 days post-transfection, cells were cultured in charcoal-stripped medium and treated with vehicle or 10 ng ml−1 IL-1β for 48 h in the presence of 1 μM 11-DHC. Western blot and quantifications of UCP1 and IL-1R1 protein levels. n = 4 per group. c, d, 10-week-old male Ucp1-Chaser-mT/mG mice were maintained on a doxycycline chow diet and administered vehicle or VX-765 (50 mg per kg per day) via daily i.p. injection for 1 week. (c) Representative IF staining of BAT for GFP (green) and perilipin (red), and DAPI (blue) in BAT (d). Quantification of BA-H percentage. n = 3 per group. e–h, 10-week-old male WT mice were housed at 24 °C or 30 °C for 1 week. The percentage of IL-1β+ cells were quantified across immune cell types, including CD45+ lymphocytes, CD45− non-immune cells (e), and CD45+CD11b+ myeloid cells and CD45+CD11b− leukocytes (f). The absolute number of IL-1β+ cells per gram of BAT (g) and per BAT fat pad (h) was quantified. n = 5 per group. i, RT–qPCR analysis of Il1b mRNA in CD45+ immune cells isolated from BAT of 10-week-old male WT mice, followed by incubation with vehicle or 1 µM NA for 4 h. n = 3 per group. Statistics were computed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test (b), unpaired two-tailed Student’s t-test (d, g, h, i), or two-way ANOVA with Šídák’s multiple-comparisons test (e, f). *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ****p < 0.0001. For b, and d–i, data are mean ± s.e.m.

a, t-SNE feature plots displaying the expression and distribution of α- and β-adrenergic receptor genes in BAT immune cells. b, c, Bone marrow neutrophils isolated from 10-week-old male WT mice were stimulated with different doses of LPS (0, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000 ng ml−1) for 6 h (b), or pretreated with different doses of NA (0, 0.1, 1, 10 µM) for 30 min, followed by LPS treatment (100 ng ml−1) for 6 h (c). RT–qPCR analysis of Il1b mRNA levels. n = 3 per group for (b) and n = 4 per group for (c). d, Bone marrow neutrophils isolated from 10-week-old male WT mice were treated with LPS (100 ng ml−1) alone or pretreated with NA (1 µM) for 30 min prior to LPS stimulation for 1, 2, 4, 6, 9 h. a, Molecular mechanism for the maintenance of the BA-L state. BA has two stable states, low and high thermogenesis, based on UCP1 expression. BA states are governed by their spatial proximity to IL-1β+ immune cells (mainly neutrophils and macrophages), which integrate signals from sympathetic neurons and immune cells to determine whether H6PD protein levels should be stabilized or degraded. Green arrows illustrate how BA-L cells are stabilized in a low-thermogenic state: IL-1β enhances the protein stability of H6PD in thermogenic adipocytes, thereby boosting the production of active glucocorticoids. Glucocorticoid activates the expression of its target RGS2, which inhibits adenylyl cyclase and reduces cAMP production, thereby reducing UCP1 expression. Red arrows illustrate how BA-L cells switch into BA-H cells upon cold exposure: cold stimulation activates sympathetic neurons, which decrease local BAT IL-1β levels; lower IL-1β levels lead to H6PD protein degradation, turning BA-L into BA-H. The purple arrow illustrates that in aged individuals, IL-1β is elevated in BAT. High IL-1β levels persistently prevent H6PD degradation, desensitizing BAs’ cold response by locking them in BA-L states. Illustration created with BioRender; Wang, Q. https://BioRender.com/basqx8x (2026). b, Bistable regulation of BA heterogeneity in a spatiotemporal manner governs thermogenic activity. We report that IL-1β-secreting immune cells, mainly neutrophils and macrophages, stabilize the surrounding BAs in a low-thermogenic state by preventing H6PD degradation; BAs farther from IL-1β+ cells are stabilized in a high-thermogenic state. Specifically, H6PD is a functional marker of BA-L cells and boosts the production of active GC. GC then activates the expression of its target, RGS2, which inhibits adenylyl cyclase, reducing cAMP production and, in turn, UCP1 expression. This bistable regulation dynamically and precisely controls cellular heterogeneity in response to signalling from sympathetic nerves and the immune system, managing thermogenesis at the tissue level. Increased IL-1β levels in the BAT of aged individuals lock BAs in a low-thermogenic state, thereby lowering thermogenic activity and leading to cold intolerance. Illustration created with BioRender; Wang, Q. https://BioRender.com/mj195m9 (2026).

#1520. EFL asks clubs to stop targeted 'banter' on social media amid fears over reputational damage in the wake of 'Spygate' fallout

Published: 09:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EST, 12 November 2026

The EFL has written to clubs calling for a halt in reputationally damaging social media posts disguised as ‘banter’ - believing the line has been blurred when it comes to regulatory matters.

The letter expressed concern over a ‘growing pattern of posts that use disputes, disciplinary matters, alleged wrongdoing or rival Clubs as material for public “banter”.’

A letter, seen by Daily Mail Sport, has been sent by EFL chief executive Trevor Birch to club chairs and executives following a board meeting.

‘While any one post may be viewed as an isolated lapse, taken together they risk creating a culture in which short-term engagement is prioritised over judgement, responsibility and long-term reputation,’ the letter read.

‘This is not about removing humour, personality or rivalry from Club channels. It is about recognising when content becomes disparaging, prolongs a dispute, targets an individual, or calls the integrity of a Club or the competition into question.

‘The impact extends beyond the Clubs directly involved. Repeated public exchanges can inflame relationships, undermine confidence in the fairness and professionalism of our competitions, and weaken the collective EFL brand.

The EFL have called for clubs to halt 'banter' social media posts. Pictured: Wrexham owners Rob Mac (left) and Ryan Reynolds (right) spoofed Southampton's Spygate case in September. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Wrexham were among the clubs to mock the case by putting a not to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors' prior to their match with Southampton on fixture release day. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Birmingham City also referenced the case by revealing the date for their fixture by showing the club badges cut into hedges and visible through binoculars. Source: X/BCFC

‘Recent media interest in perceived public disputes between Clubs illustrates how quickly individual posts can become a wider reputational issue.’

Daily Mail Sport understands the EFL are keen to avoid being seen as killjoys. Rather, they are taking a preventative approach to posts that could end up breaching FA or EFL rules.

The Southampton ‘Spygate’ scandal is among the most prominent disputes that have been referenced by clubs in social media content in recent months.

Both Birmingham City and Wrexham shared posts on the Championship fixture release date in June, using the case to highlight the dates of a fixture with Southampton.

Birmingham’s official X account posted a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into hedges which were viewed through binoculars. The account added: ‘One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on...’

Wrexham’s calendar for their matches in September included a reminder to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors’ two days before they played Southampton. An image of a man behind a tree was included in the Southampton badge.

The club also included their Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac in a spoof video in the build-up to the match. The actors were seen behind a tree similar to one which Southampton intern William Salt was caught spying near ahead of their play-off semi-final with Middlesbrough.

Following the revelations by Daily Mail Sport, Southampton were eventually thrown out of the play-offs.

Last week, Blackburn hit back at a video of West Ham manager Scott Parker declaring he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan’ by showing images of their supporters celebrating goals in their 2-1 win over the Hammers.

Blackburn hit back at West Ham boss Scott Parker last week after he declared he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan', with the club then showing supporters celebrating goals. Source: X/Rovers

The EFL reminded clubs in their letter that regulations called for clubs to ‘to act towards one another with utmost good faith’. The organisation called for clubs to consider whether their content is ‘punching down’ or ‘targeting a specific Club or individual’, adding they would likely cross the threshold if it does.

The organisation stressed that its preference is for ‘engagement and prevention’ and was not requesting clubs to make ‘bland or risk-free’ content.

However, the EFL warned it is prepared to take ‘proportionate and consistent action’ where ‘conduct which doesn’t meet the standards we expect is repeated or serious.’

Clubs have been asked to ensure a senior leader owns the standard applied to the club’s content, as well as formalising approval arrangements, briefing relevant people and exercising restraint.

#1518. Would Wayne Rooney have worked in Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona?

“I would have loved to play for Barcelona,” Wayne Rooney said recently.

“Barça beat us in the Champions League final and they didn’t have a reference No. 9. I think it would have been easy to play in that team, I would’ve fitted in perfectly.”

Well, Wayne, let us be the judge of that as we picture a world where Rooney does indeed join Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona team.

First, let’s discuss the kind of player he was.

Terrifyingly for the rest of us, there will be some football watchers who now know Rooney as a manager or a pundit more than they did as a player, so let us fill you in on what he was like on the pitch.

Simply put, Rooney was one of the best young talents ever seen in football. There were non-ridiculous comparisons between him, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.

Rooney never finished in the top three of the Ballon d’Or for his entire career, which seems mental to even think about, but if you would have asked anyone from 2005 to 2010, who the best player in the world was, he would have got a mention.

What made Rooney excellent was that he in a lot of ways a typical English striker. He is only 5ft 10’ so shorter than your average centre forward but what he lacked in going upwards, he made up for in going through.

Rooney weighed around 80kg during his United days. As a comparison, Eli Junior Kroupi is the same height and weighs 70kg. Yoane Wissa, also of a similar height, weighs 74kg.

But it was not fat that pushed Rooney up to the higher weight, it was muscle. Rio Ferdinand said Rooney had a “caveman” strength from a very young age. There are reports he was able to bench press 110 kg as a 15-year-old.

Rooney’s physicality was a nightmare for defenders to play against. We can all remember him for the reckless challenges and flying slide tackles but for every one of those, there are 20 examples of him muscling free of a defender.

A number nine who is strong isn’t groundbreaking but what separated Rooney from the pack was that he had the physicality but combined it with a technical ability rarely seen in an English centre forward.

It was his most continental ability and one that was there from very early on. Look at this goal for Everton against Arsenal, the one that had commentator Clive Tyldesley telling everyone to remember the name.

The experienced Sol Campbell gives Rooney plenty of space on the edge, for the logical reasons that this is a 16-year-old who does probably not have the confidence to be trying those kinds of shots and you would have to be a pretty good player to beat David Seaman from that range.

Given that space, Rooney looks up then picks his spot. He sidefoots it, giving it the curl needed to go up and down in the short space of time. Seaman is at full stretch and doesn’t get close to it. It kisses the bar on the way in one of the most perfectly hit shots in Premier League history.

There are countless examples of Rooney displaying the kind of technical superiority ahead of players in the league.

It was not just shooting too, Rooney was one of the best passers in the league too. His chip to Robin Van Persie in 2013 was hit hard enough to travel 40 yards in no time at all but with a delicacy that allowed it to slow and drop perfect for Van Persie, meaning the Dutchman did not have to break his stride before volleying it in.

Rooney’s ability was not lost on other players either. In 2015, he received this compliment from Xavi: “Wayne Rooney is a player I have admired for a long time. He is an extraordinary player with extraordinary capabilities.”

As well as the strength and technical ability Rooney had, he combined that with a relentlessness. Rooney grew up boxing in Merseyside, he is the footballing version of Rocky Balboa. And what that gave him was an incredible work rate. What he lacked in diet discipline over the summer, he made up in running hard yards during games, something he now laments the current United squad for failing to do.

That desire comes with a lot of positives, not least it gets the crowd on your side, but there are negatives too, such as being dragged out of position in search of the ball but also Rooney had a rawness and rashness when it came to challenges. Four club career red cards feels on the low side.

Put it all together and you have a physical, relentless player who also has the technique to play at the highest of levels. Now what about Barcelona?

The forgotten story of… Wayne Rooney’s Man Utd transfer request in 2010

The tactical philosophy of Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona has been well studied and adopted all over the world to varying degrees of success.

It was most effective at Barcelona due to being relatively in its infancy and also Guardiola was blessed with infinite talents who had been developed to play this exact style of football.

It resulted in two Champions Leagues, three league titles and the first ever sextuple. But what was it exactly?

The best example of it came in that Wembley final, when Barcelona picked apart Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United.

Tiki-taka, as it came to be known, was an evolution on the foundations laid by Johan Cruyff. It can rather falsely be labelled as pass, pass, pass but every pass in a perfect Guardiola system is with a purpose. The idea is to pull your opponent into areas they don’t want to be so that their team becomes streched, opening gaps. Being a Barcelona player is as much about running off the ball to create space for your teammate as it is what you do on it.

For players to succeed in Pep’s system, they need the combination of great passing ability, the technical quality to quickly control the ball and release and the spatial awareness to create space for their teammates via their positioning. They also need to run an awful lot.

As for what Guardiola wanted from his number nine, he very rarely played with a traditional number nine. He tried it with Zlatan Ibrahimovic and it famously did not work, although they may just as much to do with his Swedish attitude as it is with his ability.

Typically though, Guardiola wanted a number nine who could drop deep and overload the midfield. Guardiola loves his teams to exploit the half spaces between defensive lines and by having a false nine, he could operate in the area too far forward for the centre backs and too deep for the midfielders.

So the profile of player we are looking for is a technically excellent, intelligent player who can operate just as well in a 10 as he can as a nine. And that sounds a lot like Wayne Rooney.

As Rooney showed in his late career once his speed gave way, he is able to drop deep and essentially play as an advanced midfielder. At Barcelona, his move to that position may have been expedited by Guardiola’s desire to have him play as a false nine.

Rooney’s physicality would also add something new to a largely unphysical Barcelona front line. At the time they had Messi, Pedro and David Villa, three players you would not describe as overly physical, even if Messi in particular is far stronger than he often gets credited for.

There is every reason to think that Rooney would actually work very well in a Barcelona system, the only issue is one that Ibrahimovic also ran into – Messi.

For that Wembley final, Guardiola deployed Messi in the number nine spot which is where he played for the majority of the season. It was a new tactic by Guardiola as in the previous season, Messi played 39 matches on the right side compared to 12 in the centre forward position.

In 2010/11, those numbers flipped with Messi playing 43 times through the middle compared to 11 on the wing. In those 43 games, Messi scored 46 goals.

In their ideal worlds, Messi and Rooney would likely have wanted to operate in similar areas of the pitch and there would only be one winner in a potential battle for supremacy.

So while Rooney would have worked in Guardiola’s Barcelona, he would have arguably been even more impactful in Luis Enrique’s Barcelona. By the time Enrique took over, Barcelona had become much more direct and played Luis Suarez as a typical nine who could bring both Messi and Neymar into play.

Put Rooney into that system and it would have been scary.

Overall, it is fair to say that a player as technically gifted as Rooney would have definitely worked at Barcelona but he would have found himself in the shadow of Messi as so many other great players did. Still, he probably would have had a lot of trophies to help him get over that fact.

#1517. The 10 most unfootballery footballers ever: Where does James Trafford rank in weird and wonderful list?

Manchester United, Arsenal, Chelsea, Everton and Leeds United have all employed footballers who you always felt somehow stumbled into the wrong profession.

We’re talking former NASA interns, qualified doctors and those with a keen interest in literary theory. Footballers aren’t supposed to be this interesting away from the pitch, but this lot have broken the mould in weird and wonderful ways.

Here are 10 of the least footballery footballers in history.

You remember him. The 6’3″ man mountain who went viral for looking more like a minor Game of Thrones character than a professional footballer.

With a club career away from the limelight in South Korea, Greece and his native Hungary, Euro 2024 catapulted the striker in front of a whole new audience.

“Of course, one or two get to me, I usually have a laugh about it,” he said about becoming a social media sensation.

“I was born this way, I have this body shape. I’m not saying that I was this big when I was born, but I have a basic physique. Genetics – I can’t change that.”

No shade here. In a sport increasingly populated by chiselled physiques and carefully curated Instagram accounts, it’s refreshing to see a full international who looks like he should be crushing skulls in Westeros. More of them, please.

After looking into Hungary's striker, Martin Adam, I discovered:

Ádám became the top goalscorer of the 2021–22 Nemzeti Bajnokság I season, netting 31 goals.

Scored his first goal for Hungary when he aged 28 years old. His goal securing Hungary qualification.

A bit landfill indie, a bit Mod revival. You can picture Baines in Paul Weller’s backing band, wearing a parka and looking mildly unimpressed on stage for two hours.

That’s not to say he was some great footballing eccentric, but Baines had a certain individuality that stood out a bit in the identikit culture of the Barclays era.

Back in Batty’s day, it wasn’t remotely unusual for England internationals and title-winning midfielders to look and sound like blokes you’d encounter at your local.

Media training wasn’t yet a finely tuned industry, sanding down every rough edge until footballers sounded like they’d been assembled on a production line of bland platitudes. Three points, take each game as it comes, you know the rest.

Batty wasn’t alone in that respect, but his almost total disappearance from public life since retiring is a pretty good indication of how little he ever cared for the circus.

Just look at his sensationally understated response to missing a vital penalty in England’s World Cup defeat to Argentina in 1998. You’d have thought he’d misplaced his car keys.

“You know what the position is before you step up and take a pen,” he said.

“I’m disappointed it didn’t work out right but I’m pleased I took one.”

Nevin isn’t the only footballer with a penchant for indie music, but his credentials go well beyond owning a few Smiths records.

He’s a brilliant broadcaster and his genuine enthusiasm for the game always shines through, but we still get the feeling that running down the wing for Chelsea and Everton denied him his true calling of playing keyboards for a Glaswegian dreampop band.

Once did a Peel session, supported the Cocteau Twins, reunited for a run of shows at 200-capacity venues back in 2016. He can but dream.

READ: All hail James Trafford: How the most normal bloke in elite football became England’s No.1

We can’t be certain, but we’re pretty sure that Hislop is the only 90s Premier League cult hero that could’ve worked for NASA. Let us reach out to Tony Yeboah and Georgi Kinkladze and get back to you.

“I had been attending university in the US on a football scholarship, and had been doing a summer internship at NASA the year before I graduated,” Hislop reminisced in an interview with FourFourTwo.

“After getting my degree in Mechanical Engineering, I was drafted by an indoor team called the Baltimore Blast. This was before the days of MLS. As it turned out, Baltimore were touring England that summer.

“We played Aston Villa in two indoor games. Dwight Yorke – another Trinidadian – had signed for them a couple of years previously.”

The Jacques Brel-inspired crooner album he released? The Ken Loach film he appeared in? Suddenly retiring at the age of 30 just because? Basically every word he’s ever uttered?

None of it at all footballery. We’re still not entirely convinced he was a real person. Some sort of post-rave collective fever dream apparition.

In a recent appearance on the Second Captains podcast, Bellerin delved into his admiration for Stefan Zweig, the Austrian literary giant known for his nuanced character studies and literary explorations of obsession, morality and the human psyche.

This guy used to line up alongside Andrea Pirlo and David Villa.

Never seen someone look less like a footballer pic.twitter.com/CQkp921ziW

Socrates was destined to be different from the very beginning. His father was a self-educated intellectual with a passion for philosophy and literature, and named his first three sons after figures from ancient Greece. His brothers were called Sostenes and Sofocles.

One formative childhood memory was watching his father dispose of his treasured library following Brazil’s 1964 military coup. He was 10 years old at the time.

As an adult, he became a qualified doctor, was an outspoken political activist and helped spearhead a revolutionary movement at Corinthians. He’d have been just as comfortable discussing Marxism over a bottle of red as he was dictating the tempo in midfield.

He smoked two packs of cigarettes a day, sported a magnificent beard, captained Brazil at two World Cups and briefly came out of retirement to rock up at Garforth Town.

Football has produced plenty of superstars, but precious few quite like Socrates. Almost certainly the coolest footballer in history.

#1515. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1513. Man United set to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach: Club make formal approach to US Soccer after agreeing personal terms - with Michael Carrick's exit confirmed on Thursday

Published: 03:10 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 12:15 EST, 12 November 2026

Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as head coach to replace Michael Carrick following a day of talks over both men.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Meanwhile, the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick’s departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino’s appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager - but he took training as usual on Wednesday

Pochettino, who has managed Southampton,Tottenham, and Chelsea, will succeed Michael Carrick

Carrick checked in at Carrington at 7.45am on Wednesday with his fate in the balance

He was pictured leaving Manchester United's training base at around 1.15pm

Pochettino is pictured working on United States national team duty on Tuesday (Source: X/USMNT)

The second leg is Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

Amid the secret talks between United and Pochettino’s camp on Wednesday, there was more intrigue when the federation cancelled media access to the players at late notice but allowed cameras to film an open training session.

Sources said the decision was made out of respect for Veterans Day in America, but it also meant the players didn’t have to field any awkward questions over their coach’s future.

Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams was quoted by the US media as saying: ‘Why would his name not be on it (United’s list)?

Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are meeting in Monaco for talks today

The United execs meet in Monaco today (Pictured is the Casino Monte-Carlo in Monaco)

‘I mean, the credibility, the resume speaks for itself. It goes to show for us how lucky we are to be able to work under a manager of his quality and the person he is.’

Meanwhile, Berrada and Wilcox flew back to Manchester from Nice on Wednesday with United expected to announce Carrick’s departure imminently after 10 months in charge.

The 45-year-old took training at Carrington for the second day running, arriving at 7.45am and leaving shortly after 1.30pm.

However, it has been clear for some days that Carrick would lose his job after United dropped into the relegation zone following the club’s worst start in 40 years.

#1511. The top goalscorers for club & country in 2026 so far: Kane, Yamal, Mbappe, Raphinha…

Big names from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Arsenal and Bayern Munich feature alongside some surprise names in the most prolific goalscorers of the calendar year so far.

Some big names are surprisingly absent from the most prolific goalscorers of 2026 to date.

Drawn from Europe’s five major leagues, here are the top 10 goalscorers in 2026 across club and international competitions.

Schick has had reason to celebrate in 2026. Earlier this year, he reached the milestone of 100 goals for Bayer Leverkusen.

He’s been on fire this season, with 12 goals from 14 games for the German side.

There won’t be any more international goals from Schick, though. He retired from Czech Republic duty after the World Cup.

The jury is still out on Gyokeres, who remains a perplexing forward.

This calendar year has seen him look borderline anonymous and increasingly sidelined at Arsenal.

And yet Gyokeres also fired Sweden to the World Cup with a hat-trick against Ukraine and a late winner against Poland. He’s basically the Ikea Gerd Muller at this point.

What a year it’s been for Malen. Started it as a benchwarmer at Aston Villa. Set to finish it as one of Europe’s most lethal strikers at Roma.

Malen made an immediate impact after his January move to the Italian capital and his scoring rate has barely slowed down since.

For some reason, his form hasn’t quite translated into international football; he hasn’t scored for the Netherlands at all this year.

But high-flying Roma are laughing. Malen almost won the Serie A golden boot last season despite arriving midway through and he’s a leading contender for the gong this season.

A surprise entry, perhaps, given his struggles for Real Madrid.

The Brazilian has scored just one La Liga goal so far this season, and his goalscoring has been downright ordinary for Los Blancos for quite some time now.

He’s scored 18 goals in all competitions for his club this calendar year, averaging out at a not-great average of one every 186 minutes. His Brazil team-mate Raphinha, by contrast, has averaged a goal every 70 minutes for Barcelona in 2026.

But his international exploits look considerably more impressive, while his five goals in this international break – two against Japan, a hat-trick against Singapore – come after five goals at the World Cup. He’s scored 11 goals in 14 appearances for the Selecao in 2026.

Vini’s place in Jose Mourinho’s favoured XI has come under threat from summer signing Yan Diomande. Going back to his club refreshed, with his confidence boosted, might just be what he needs.

A fairly recent entrant into the top 10 after heading into the international break on the back of a hat trick against Union Berlin.

Olise was the Bundesliga’s best assister last season but has been more than capable of finding the net himself a fair few times too.

He didn’t score any goals at the World Cup but netted the winner in Zinedine Zidane’s second game in charge of France. The best Fantasy Footballer around right now.

Yamal has long been talked up as a Ballon d’Or contender, and slowly but surely he’s getting the numbers to back it up.

The teenager’s goalscoring output has grown season on season, and 2025-26 was no exception. February’s hat-trick against Villarreal was evidence of a player about to go truly stratospheric.

Unfortunately, the final furlong of the campaign was hit by a hamstring injury, or else we suspect he’d be a few places higher up in this list.

He needed just 10 minutes in his first World Cup start to find the back of the net, although that would be his only goal in Spain’s triumph out in North America.

Now he’s looking fit and hungry – at least based on the evidence of his exceptional form of late.

The Brazilian has an exceptional tally of 33 goals for Barcelona so far this calendar year (plus one for Brazil), which is especially impressive when you consider he’s missed quite a lot of action due to injury.

He averages a goal every 49 minutes for Barca this season – to put that in context, Kylian Mbappe averages a goal every 84 minutes for Real Madrid.

Raphinha has scored in all but three of the Barca games he’s played in in 2026-27, scoring hat tricks in two, and currently leads the Europe-wide goalscoring charts with 15 in the league.

The top three are the last three winners of the European Golden Shoe. This list has taken a while to take shape, but the frontrunners are the usual suspects.

Haaland’s four goals against Iraq and Senegal in the group stages finally saw him climb up into the top 10, from which he was surprisingly absent in the latter half of the 2025-26 club season, before he added to his World Cup tally against the Ivory Coast. Then there were two goals against Brazil.

He finally drew a blank as Norway exited the World Cup at the hands of England at the quarter-final stage. He earned a well-deserved rest before spearheading Man City’s new era under Enzo Maresca.

Same as it ever was with nine goals in nine Premier League appearances for City this season, plus braces against Porto and PSG and another Champions League goal against his favourite opponents, RB Leipzig.

Like his rival Haaland, it somehow took Mbappe until mid-June to enter the top 10.

Mbappe kicked off the year in superb style, scoring in six successive starts for Real Madrid (nine goals in total) before dipping considerably with just one goal in his next seven appearances.

By the nature of his 10 goals at the World Cup, we don’t expect to see the Real Madrid superstar dropping back out. His Champions League record is pretty sensational.

Arguably the finest player in world football right now. How often have you been able to say that about an Englishman?

The only player in Europe’s five major leagues to average a better-than-goal-a-game output so far this calendar year, the England captain has 41 goals in 40 appearances for Bayern Munich in all competitions in 2026 – including home and away against Real Madrid and PSG.

He capped off his superb season with a hat-trick in the DFB Pokal final. Two goals against Croatia showed Kane carried his form into the World Cup, where he eventually scored six times.

Unbelievably, the Norway game was Kane’s first knockout appearance for club and country in 2025-26 in which he didn’t score. Which, of course, he followed with a blank against Argentina.

Surprisingly enough, Kane failed to add to his tally by drawing a blank in his first three Bayern appearances of the 2026-27 campaign.

But it’s back to normal service with his Bayern tally standing at 10 goals in 14 games. The Czechs and Croatia have been on the receiving end in the Nations League too.

Still some way to go before catching Lionel Messi’s calendar year record, mind.
